paragraphs: City of Wolverhampton Council recruits and supports its own carers through its Fostering for Wolverhampton service. The council reported that in March 2023 there were 218 fostering households caring for 274 local children and young people, while 104 children lived with independent agency foster parents, such as those listed on this page.

The council asks carers to live within about 20 miles of the city and to have a spare bedroom, and says assessment can take as little as 16 weeks. It has appealed in particular for carers who can keep brothers and sisters together, and in the right circumstances it can help sibling carers buy a larger vehicle.

Carers receive a regular tax-exempt fee and allowance. New carers are matched with an experienced foster parent through a buddy system, supervising social workers give closer support in the first weeks of a placement, and help is available around the clock. The council also runs social events and a peer support network for its carers.
Before deciding, compare what the council offers with two or three of the agencies below, and ask each about pay, training and support in Wolverhampton.
